info.name: EGOVHelper — signer + eGov Mobile QR
info.description:
End-to-end test collection for the egov-helper signer service and the SIGEX QR + eGov Mobile flow.

What's in here
---------------
1. **Backend (Kalkan signer)** — `/health`, `/sign`, `/info`, `/cms/inspect` against your locally running Java service (default `http://localhost:7575`).
2. **QR + eGov Mobile (SIGEX hub)** — `POST /api/egovQr`, the `dataURL` submit, and the `signURL` poll. Lets you walk the eGov Mobile signing flow from Postman without a browser.
3. **Identity check via QR** — chains `POST /api/egovQr` (you scan the QR with eGov Mobile) → poll for CMS → `POST /cms/inspect` to extract the signer's BIN/IIN.

The environment ships with the real Elorda.com GOST-512 `.p12` (base64) and password pre-filled so teammates can run requests as-is. **Do not commit the environment file with the password in plain text — see README.md.**

item.name: 1. Backend (Kalkan signer)
item.description:
The Java service in `packages/java/egov-helper-signer/`. Start it locally with `mvn package && java -jar target/egov-helper-signer.jar` — it listens on port 7575 by default.

These endpoints expect a `.p12` and password from the user. We use the real Elorda.com GOST-512 cert so the team can verify the full Kalkan signing path (GOST keys cannot be tested via the browser-only RSA flow).

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns `{ ok: true, kalkan: "KALKAN/x.y" }` once the service is ready. If `kalkan` is `"(not loaded)"`, the Kalkan JAR is missing from `libs/`.

exec: // Capture the CMS into env so /cms/inspect can run next without copy-paste.
console.log('Signed. CMS length =', json.signatureBase64.length, '| cert BIN =', json.certInfo?.bin, '| IIN =', json.certInfo?.iin);

request.description:
Loads the `.p12`, signs `documentBase64`, returns a CAdES-BES CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData blob.

- For GOST keys (like Elorda.com) `hashAlgorithm` is ignored — the curve mandates the hash.
- `detached: true` (recommended) returns signature only; verifier needs the original doc.
- `detached: false` embeds the document inside the CMS.

The test script stores `signatureBase64` into `{{cmsBase64}}` and the cert's BIN/IIN into `{{certBin}}` / `{{certIin}}` so you can run `/cms/inspect` immediately after.

exec: console.log('Cert subject — BIN:', json.bin, '| IIN:', json.iin, '| CN:', json.commonName, '| Org:', json.organization);

request.description:
Loads the `.p12`, returns just the parsed certificate subject (BIN/IIN/CN/organization/key usage/validity/serial/PEM). Same body shape as `/sign` for protocol uniformity; the document fields are ignored.

This is what `checkBin()` in the JS lib calls — it's the BIN-match check before committing to a real signing flow.

item.name: POST /cms/inspect — extract cert info from a CMS blob

exec: console.log('Signer subject — BIN:', json.bin, '| IIN:', json.iin, '| CN:', json.commonName);

request.description:
Parses a CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData blob and returns the signer's cert info (BIN/IIN/CN/etc.). Does NOT verify the signature value — purely a "what's in this CMS" query.

Used by the JS lib's `checkBinViaQr()` to extract cert info from a CMS produced by eGov Mobile via the SIGEX QR flow — so the BIN/IIN can be compared against the user-typed value without ever asking for a `.p12`.

Pre-flight: run `POST /sign` or the QR flow first so `{{cmsBase64}}` is populated.

Full cryptographic verification of a CMS against the original document.

Returns three independent booleans per signer:
- `signatureValid` — signature value verifies against the embedded cert's public key.
- `documentDigestMatches` — SHA / Stribog hash of `documentBase64` matches the `messageDigest` signed attribute in the CMS.
- `certValidAtSigningTime` — the `signingTime` attribute is within the cert's NotBefore/NotAfter window.

Overall `valid` is `true` iff all three pass for every signer.

For a **detached** CMS (eGov Mobile, `CMS_SIGN_ONLY`) you MUST pass `documentBase64`. For **attached** CMS (`CMS_WITH_DATA`) it's optional — if you pass it, the endpoint checks the doc matches what's embedded.

Pre-flight: run `POST /sign` (or the full QR flow) first so `{{cmsBase64}}` is populated; `{{documentBase64}}` should be the same bytes you signed.

item.name: POST /cms/verify (legal doc) — fetch PDF by role/type/version/language

request.description:
Atasuai legal-docs integration. Instead of sending the document bytes, you send four params and the signer service fetches the canonical PDF from:

```
{{LEGAL_DOC_BASE_URL}}?role={{legalDocRole}}&type={{legalDocType}}&version={{legalDocVersion}}&language={{legalDocLanguage}}
```

The server hashes the fetched bytes and compares to the CMS's messageDigest, producing the same response as the inline-doc variant. `documentSource` in the response will be `legal:<role>/<type>/<version>/<language>` so you can confirm exactly which doc was checked.

Server-side prerequisites:
- `LEGAL_DOC_BASE_URL` env var must be set on the signer (e.g. `https://atasuai.example.com/legal/api/contract/pdf`).
- The legal-docs endpoint must return the PDF body with HTTP 200.

Client-side prerequisites:
- `{{cmsBase64}}` populated (run `/sign` or the QR flow first).
- The four `legalDoc*` env vars set to the same role/type/version/language the user signed.

item.name: 2. QR + eGov Mobile (SIGEX hub)
item.description:
The eGov Mobile signing path goes through the public SIGEX hub at `https://sigex.kz`. Normally the browser drives this (via `sigex-qr-signing-client`), but you can walk the protocol from Postman to debug or to simulate the flow end-to-end with a real phone.

**Run order**
  1. `POST /api/egovQr` → captures `qrCode`, `dataURL`, `signURL`, `eGovMobileLaunchLink` into env vars.
  2. `POST {{dataURL}}` → submit the document(s) to sign.
  3. Render `{{qrCode}}` somewhere and scan with eGov Mobile (or on a phone, open `{{eGovMobileLaunchLink}}`).
  4. `GET {{signURL}}` → poll until the CMS array arrives. Each entry is one signature, base64.

exec: console.log('  (qrCode is base64 PNG, see {{qrCode}} — render at https://www.base64-image.de/ or similar to scan.)');

request.description:
Registers a new QR signing session on the SIGEX hub. Response shape:
```json
{
  "qrCode": "<base64 PNG>",
  "dataURL": "https://sigex.kz/api/.../data",
  "signURL": "https://sigex.kz/api/.../sign",
  "eGovMobileLaunchLink": "egovmobile://...",
  "eGovBusinessLaunchLink": "egovbusiness://..."
}
```

The test script captures all five into env vars so the next two requests can use them as `{{dataURL}}` and `{{signURL}}`.

`{{$isoTimestamp}}` is a Postman dynamic variable — gives each session a fresh description.

exec: console.log('Data uploaded to SIGEX. Now scan the QR (or open {{eGovMobileLaunchLink}} on your phone) and sign in eGov Mobile.');

request.description:
Uploads the document(s) the user is about to sign to the SIGEX hub.

- `signMethod`: `CMS_SIGN_ONLY` (detached signature — recommended) or `CMS_WITH_DATA` (attached, doc embedded inside CMS).
- `documentsToSign[].document.file.data` is base64 of the file bytes. We reuse `{{documentBase64}}` so the QR flow signs the same payload as the `.p12` /sign request above.

After this returns 200, the QR is hot — render `{{qrCode}}` and have the user scan it with eGov Mobile, or open `{{eGovMobileLaunchLink}}` on the phone where they're already authenticated.

exec: // Response is either { signatures: [base64, ...] } when ready, or an empty/in-progress payload while we wait.
console.log('Now run "POST /cms/inspect" in folder 1 to extract the signer cert info.');
console.log('Not signed yet — re-run this request after the user signs in eGov Mobile.');

request.description:
Polls the SIGEX hub for the signature(s). Re-run repeatedly (every 1–2s) until `signatures` is a non-empty array.

Each entry in `signatures` is a base64-encoded CMS / PKCS#7 SignedData blob. The test script captures the first one into `{{cmsBase64}}` — feed it into `POST /cms/inspect` to read the signer's BIN/IIN out of the cert.

The SIGEX session has a finite TTL (a few minutes); if the user never signs, the poll eventually returns an expired-session error.

item.name: 3. Full identity check via QR (chained)
item.description:
Walk a complete checkBinViaQr() flow from Postman:

  1. **Register QR session** (`POST /api/egovQr` from folder 2). Captures `dataURL`, `signURL`, `qrCode`.
  2. **Submit a challenge document** (`POST {{dataURL}}` from folder 2). The doc here is `documentBase64` — but for a real BIN check you typically sign a short throwaway like `"BIN verification — <ISO timestamp>"`. Use the **Sign throwaway challenge** request below if you want to override.
  3. **Render the QR or open the deeplink** — `{{qrCode}}` (base64 PNG) for desktop scan, or `{{eGovMobileLaunchLink}}` for same-device.
  4. **Poll** (`GET {{signURL}}`) until a signature comes back.
  5. **Inspect the CMS** — the request below calls `POST /cms/inspect` on your Java backend and compares the embedded BIN/IIN against the typed value `{{expectedBin}}`. Mirrors the logic of `checkBinViaQr()` in [src/bin.ts](../../../src/bin.ts).

exec: if (certBin && certBin === typed) { match = true; matchedField = 'BIN'; }
else if (certIin && certIin === typed) { match = true; matchedField = 'IIN'; }
pm.test('typed value matches cert BIN/IIN', () => pm.expect(match).to.eql(true));

request.description:
Last step of the QR identity-check chain.

Pre-flight:
- `{{cmsBase64}}` must be populated (run the QR poll in folder 2 until it returns a signature, or run `POST /sign` first).
- `{{expectedBin}}` should be the 12-digit BIN/IIN the user typed in your UI.

The test script compares `{{expectedBin}}` against the cert's BIN, then its IIN. Asserts a match — fails the test if the typed value matches neither.

item.name: Step 6 — POST /cms/verify (proves user signed THIS doc)

request.description:
Optional follow-up to Step 5. Step 5 only checks the BIN matches a cert — but anyone could have signed an arbitrary doc with that cert. This step is the cryptographic proof that the holder of `{{certBin}}`'s private key signed THIS specific `{{documentBase64}}` and that the cert was valid at the time.

Use this for: real signing flows where you store the CMS as legal evidence.
For identity-only checks (BIN verification): Step 5 alone is enough — you don't care about the throwaway challenge's signature beyond the cert it exposes.

exec: // Sanity checks on the environment before every request.
console.warn('signerBaseUrl is empty — set it to your egov-helper-signer URL (default http://localhost:7575).');
console.warn('p12Base64 / p12Password are empty — the /sign and /info requests will fail. Import the EGOVHelper.postman_environment.json environment.');
